fixed_before: holdout v3 student and sentence selection, annotation, and any holdout v3 prediction

data.excluded_students: the 25 students of cell_reliability_holdout_v1 and the 36 students of cell_reliability_holdout_v2, both opened on 2026-11-06; selection runs on the 37 remaining holdout students
data.selection: the same CELL pilot procedure (src/cell_pilot.py) as holdout v1 and v2: structural metadata for students, parser-derived structural categories for sentences; no labels, verdicts, predictions, quality, length, or duplicate flags
data.reserve: none: this batch uses every remaining holdout student, so no untouched CELL holdout data is left after it is opened

parse.pipeline: frozen en_core_web_sm 3.8.0 with spaCy 3.8.13 (sentence segmentation v1)
parse.context: each sentence is a span of its complete essay parse
parse.reference_parse: en_core_web_trf 3.8.0 (spacy-curated-transformers 0.3.0, torch 2.15.0) on the complete essay text, used only by Syntax Reliability v1.5; the labeller never sees it

annotation.labeller: a new separate model session (annotator_id claude_sealed_holdout_v3) that sees only a blind packet: sentence, neighbouring sentences, sm token parse, clause heads, and the annotation guideline
labeller_must_not_see: Syntax Reliability verdicts or flags of any version
Reliability ML features, probabilities, or predictions
development results, error analyses, holdout v1 and v2 results, and project history
annotation.owner_review: the dataset owner reviews every UNRELIABLE, MOSTLY_RELIABLE, and NOT_ANALYZABLE label and a seeded random sample of 40 RELIABLE labels (seed 20261107); reviewed records become adjudicated by human_owner_v1
annotation.freeze: labels are locked by file hash before the evaluation run; no label changes after the run

systems.reference: Syntax Reliability v1.2 warning (medium or low)
systems.primary_candidate: Syntax Reliability v1.5 warning (medium or low), compared with v1.4 to isolate the reference_parse_nominal_clause_head signal
secondary_candidates: Syntax Reliability v1.3, v1.4, and v1.5 warnings, each compared with v1.2
Reliability ML Model B, refit on all 606 development observations with the threshold chosen by the heuristic_precision rule exactly as in holdout v1 and v2 (expected 0.9238), compared with v1.2
not_evaluated: Clause Detection v2.2 and sentence segmentation v2, whose labels would need re-judging
the other reference-parse variants explored on development data

analysis.analysis_set: labelled analyzable sentences where v1.2 does not abstain; abstentions are counted and reported separately
metrics: true and false positive and negative counts
analysis.paired_comparison: discordant counts on UNRELIABLE sentences (recall) and on usable sentences (false warnings), each with a two-sided exact McNemar test, for v1.5 against v1.4 and for v1.3, v1.4, v1.5, and Model B against v1.2
analysis.primary_question: Does the transformer reference-parse warning raise recall over v1.4 without adding false warnings?
analysis.decision_rule: the v1.5 signal is confirmed if its recall gain over v1.4 on UNRELIABLE sentences is significant (exact McNemar p < 0.05) and it adds no significant false warnings; if v1.5 adds significant false warnings or loses catches, the result is negative and the transformer check is withdrawn from analyze_writing and the CLI; otherwise the result is inconclusive and the check stays optional as a development candidate. In every case v1.4 stays the default, because v1.5 needs the optional transformer model
analysis.power_note: on the 600 development sentences the signal fired on 16 (14 UNRELIABLE), adding 8 catches and 2 false warnings over v1.4; the signal was chosen from four variants on those sentences, so the development gain is optimistic. Holdout v2 had 23 UNRELIABLE sentences with a non-finite failure among 362, 18 of them missed by v1.4; with no lost catches a significant result needs at least 6 new catches
analysis.no_pooling: holdout v1, v2, and v3 are reported separately; earlier batches were opened before v1.5 existed and are not re-scored as untouched data

opening_procedure: freeze this plan, the evaluated code, the optional transformer requirements, and the development set lock in git

prepare the batch, write the blind packet, and label it in a new sealed session; owner review follows in that session, with the review sheet built by scripts/review_cell_annotation_labels.py --seed 20261107 (its default seed belongs to holdout v1)
lock the holdout v3 labels by hash
record the opening in split_v1.json (holdout_openings) and in PROJECT_HISTORY.md
run the evaluation once and report every planned number, whatever the outcome
after opening, no CELL holdout student is untouched; later reliability changes need new independent data
